tier_reason: benchmark_url (webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk) and every other source (alglib.net, plato.asu.edu, coin-or.org GAMSlinks, osti.gov, sandia.gov, gnu.org) fail with ENOTFOUND here, so the GLPK-vs-lp_solve numbers are known only from WebSearch snippets; per the snippet-only rule the tier stays at C. The underlying data look like Mittelmann's independent LP benchmarks (the slides say so, snippet only), so a retier to B is possible once plato.asu.edu or the slides can be opened.

corrections.claimed_speedup: HiGHS-team slides (Hall, INFORMS 2019; snippet only, tables said to be drawn from Mittelmann's LP benchmarks), relative time, lower is better. 17 March 2019 table (Clp = 1): HiGHS 5.3, GLPK 26, lp_solve 112, so GLPK about 4.3x faster than lp_solve (derived from page data). 4 June 2019 table (COPT = 1): Clp 1.3, GLPK 24.0, lp_solve 92.2, about 3.8x (derived from page data). 9 October 2019 table (COPT = 1, not Clp): Clp 1.4, QSopt 26, GLPK 28, lp_solve 108, about 3.9x (derived from page data), with GLPK solving 31 instances against lp_solve's 23. ALGLIB benchmark over 90 NETLIB LPs (snippet only): ALGLIB, HiGHS and Clp roughly equal, GLPK roughly 2x behind them, lp_solve roughly 3x behind, so GLPK about 1.5x faster than lp_solve (derived from page data). Sandia report SAND2013-8847 (2013, snippet only): lp_solve considerably slower than GLPK and failed on several test problems; no ratio seen.
corrections.stars_or_usage: GNU package, shipped in Debian/Ubuntu, openSUSE, Oracle Linux EPEL and OpenBSD ports (search snippets); the only GitHub copy found, github.com/firedrakeproject/glpk, is a one-commit 4.60 snapshot with 57 stars and 31 forks, archived 2025-06-16, not the official source
corrections.caveats: SNIPPET ONLY: every numbers page (webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk slides, alglib.net, plato.asu.edu, coin-or.org GAMSlinks LP benchmarks, osti.gov and sandia.gov for SAND2013-8847) and gnu.org itself fail with ENOTFOUND in this sandbox; table values, test set, hardware and solver versions were taken from WebSearch summaries and were not seen on the pages. The HiGHS slide tables change their reference solver (Clp = 1 in March 2019, COPT = 1 in June and October 2019), and the 'time' column is probably Mittelmann's scaled shifted geometric mean in which unsolved instances count at the time limit, so part of lp_solve's gap reflects its failures (23 solved against GLPK's 31 in October 2019). The same sources rank GLPK far behind the current open-source leaders (about 20x slower than Clp and about 5x slower than HiGHS on the slides; about 2x behind ALGLIB, HiGHS and Clp on ALGLIB's NETLIB set; a 2020 HiGHS table puts GLPK at 54 against Clp's 1), and the Sandia 2013 report found GLPK could not match Clp or CPLEX; neither HiGHS nor Clp is in the catalog yet. The only win is over lp_solve, the slowest solver in those sets. The slides are by HiGHS's authors and ALGLIB's page by a competing commercial vendor, though both are third parties to GLPK and lp_solve. An unverified Medium post claims GLPK beats Clp and HiGHS on a few large LPs (woodw, pilot, pds-20). The GLPK FAQ's claim of beating lp_solve 4.0 'in many cases' has no numbers. GLPK has no public version-control repository; the last release found is 5.0, announced on info-gnu on 2020-12-16 (snippet only), with no later release seen. Category sparse-and-solvers chosen over the lead's guessed blas-lapack because GLPK is an LP/MIP solver.

notes: Kept at C: GLPK beats lp_solve by about 3.8-4.3x on the Mittelmann-derived HiGHS slide tables and by about 1.5x on ALGLIB's NETLIB set, all from snippets because every source host is blocked. Main shortcomings: snippet-only evidence, slow against Clp (about 20x) and HiGHS (about 5x), no public VCS, last release 5.0 in December 2020 (not corrected to 'abandoned' because the release list could not be opened), and the lp_solve ratio is inflated by lp_solve's failed instances. Leads: HiGHS (ERGO-Code/HiGHS) and COIN-OR Clp are the faster open-source LP solvers and are not catalogued; Mittelmann's plato.asu.edu LP benchmarks and SAND2013-8847 are retier sources if they become reachable.
